rated_messages.input_message: Instead of smoking, keep your fingers busy by scrolling through your phone.
Take a minute to notice what the urge feels like in your body without smoking a cigarette. Notice what is going on. See what happens. Does the urge pass?

Write down why you want to stop smoking to resist a craving. Remember, trying something to beat the urge is always better than doing nothing. Each time you resist a cig, you're one step closer to being tobacco-free.

You don't have to act on this feeling by smoking or doing anything about it. Give it some space, breathe, and see if it changes. Let the urge and feeling be there while you focus on doing something you care about.
Whenever you think about smoking, listen to your favorite song and sing it out loud!

Some people find it helpful to give a name to their urge. If you're experiencing regular urges, give that feeling a name ('Olga the urge'?), and tell it that you won't give in to it. It may make it easier to live with (e.g. "ok Olga, I need to be by myself now...").
If you are tempted to smoke by being in this location, see if you can sit with that temptation for 1 minute. When the minute is over, do it again. Soon, it should pass.
To help get through a 'risky situation', remind yourself of how far you've come and the effort that you've put in. Don't ruin your hard work - stay strong!
Think of your anxious mind like a toddler throwing a tantrum. The best way to respond is to quietly watch, but not give in.
Try to stop smoking by setting yourself a rule. For example, "IF I am tempted, THEN I will chew on some mints" - make your own rule that will work for you.
